claims.text: Retention or loss of toughness in high-entropy alloys is governed by competition between dislocation-mediated plasticity and grain-boundary-mediated fracture.
Alloy composition, processing conditions, and microstructure influence the competition between dislocation-mediated plasticity and grain-boundary-mediated fracture.
Varying the concentration of a specific element can serve as a controlled intervention.
Changing heat treatment or mechanical deformation can serve as a controlled processing intervention.
The proposed operating range extends from -200°C to 1000°C.
The proposed strain-rate range extends from 10^-3 to 10^3 s^-1.
The proposed stress states extend from uniaxial to multiaxial loading.
Grain boundaries and dislocation networks play a crucial role in mediating plasticity and fracture.
Composition and processing conditions that enhance dislocation-mediated plasticity will increase toughness relative to the baseline.
Conditions that promote grain-boundary-mediated fracture will decrease toughness relative to the baseline.
Baseline toughness can be measured using standardized Charpy impact or tensile testing.
The hypothesis should hold within the stated temperature and strain-rate ranges and within specified alloy-composition ranges.
The hypothesis may not apply outside the proposed ranges or under extreme loading conditions.
A combination of mechanical testing, electron microscopy, X-ray diffraction, and finite-element modeling could test the hypothesis.
A lack of correlation between composition, processing conditions, and toughness would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of finite-element modeling to capture the observed behavior would falsify the mechanistic hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary invokes specified alloy-composition ranges, but no numerical or categorical composition range is provided.

The intervention proposes several alternative changes without selecting a specific element, concentration increment, heat treatment, or deformation schedule, while the experiment does not identify which one will be controlled.
